t: Tang namar ba [clause], ym mut ba [clause]
ex: Tang namar ba ka dor jrong, ym mut ba ka kham bha.
n: ym mut ba = it doesn't mean that.

ex: Nga sngewthuh ïa phi, hynrei nga dang pyrkhat ba ngi dei ban ap.
Nga sngewthuh balei phi sngewsih. Kata ka la long kaba ym hok eh.
n: hok = fair, right.

ex: Tang nga, ne ka khriat eh hapoh kane?
n: Informal; the tag ne (or) carries the check.

ex: Phi yn pyrkhat ba ka hotel kaba dor jrong kumne kan don ka Wi-Fi kaba bha.
n: Flag: literal 'you would think'; speakers also say lada ka dor jrong kumne, ... hi?

ex: Phi la thiah tang lai kynta? Kumta hi phi thait.
n: Kumta hi (that's why) is the natural 'no wonder'.

ex: Wat ong ba phi la duh biang ïa ki chabi.
Phi ong ba phim pat ju ïohi ïa ka ïthah?
n: Said with rising disbelief; add shisha? for force.

ex: Map, nga la pyrkhat ba ka meeting ka long ha lai baje.
n: la pyrkhat ba (I had thought that) is the polite admission.

ex: Nga la tip shisha ba nga la buh ïa ka phone halor ka miej.
Nga pyrkhat ba phim shym la sngewtynnad ïa ka phlim, hooid?
n: The tag hooid? turns it into a checked inference.

ex: Nga dang sdang pyrkhat ba um wan.
Ha pdeng lynti sha airport, nga la kynmaw ba nga la klet ïa ka passport.
n: kynmaw = realise, remember.

ex: Ka jingim ka kham ban tang ka kam, phi tip.
n: Flag: no neat idiom; literally 'life is more than just work'.

ex: Ngam lyngngoh lada kan slap mynta ka miet.
n: Snow adapted to rain.

ex: Wat sngewsih shaphang ka slap. Ka dei ban phai bha shwa ka sngi pdeng.
n: dei ban = is sure to / should.

ex: Kumba nga tip ïa u para jong nga, un poi lait shi kynta.
Nga tip ei, u dang thiah.
n: Flag: 'who knows' sense; lehse (maybe) ... ruh is also used.

ex: Ym don uba tip katno kan jrong ka lain.
Kaei ka ïadei ka rta jong nga bad kane?
n: rta = age.

ex: Ngam pat shaniah ba kane ka dei ka por kaba bha ban thied ïing.
n: shaniah = trust, be convinced.

ex: U ong ba un ïeh ban dih duma? Ngan ngeit haba ngan ïohi.
n: ngeit = believe.

ex: Lada ka ïing bam ka dap, ngi lah ruh ban order sha ïing.
Ka bas kam wan. Kham bha ngi ïaid kjat hi.
Ngam ju pynkhein, hynrei kane ka soup ka khriat.
n: Flag: literally 'I don't usually ...'; pynkhein = complain.

t: Kan ym long eiei lada phi [base-verb]
ex: Kan ym long eiei lada phi phone lypa ban kylli lada ki plie.
Lada phim tip kaei ban order, ka pasta ka bha man ka por.
n: Literally 'is good every time'.

ex: Ym don daw ban kren sniew ïa u nongai jingbam.
Wat la kumno, wat ïathuh ïa u kpa shaphang ka party.
Wat shisha bam ïa ka cake kaba sah!
n: Informal and emphatic; the tone does most of the work.

ex: Ym donkam ban phone ïa u. Um ju shim.
To ngi ong ba ngin mih ha phra baje. Kan biang?
Lah ban ong ba ka party ka la bha shisha.

t: Nga la kwah ban kylli lada phi kwah ban [base-verb]
ex: Nga la kwah ban kylli lada phi kwah ban leit bam ja lang ha ka sngi Friday.
Nga biang na ka bynta ka phlim mynta ka miet, lada me ruh.
n: Flag: literal 'I'm ready for'; nga mynjur (I'm in) also works.

t: ban kylli ïa kiwei ki doktor
ex: U doktor dat u ong ba nga donkam ka crown, hynrei nga kwah ban kylli ïa uwei pat u doktor.
n: No set phrase; ask another doctor.

t: ki jingjia bym bha na ka dawai
ex: Don ki jingjia bym bha na kane ka dawai ba nga dei ban tip?
n: Flag: descriptive; Shillong speakers usually say 'side effect' in English.

ex: Nga thait eh hadien ka jingkynriah ïing.
n: thait = tired.

ex: Ap khyndiat, ai nga shongthiah khyndiat.
n: Literally 'rest a little' to get your breath back.

ex: Map ïa nga ba nga la bam bhiar ïa phi mynhynnin.
n: Flag: bam bhiar/sngew bitar (get angry); leh jhieh is also heard. Pick one you hear locally.

ex: Wat tieng eh, hynrei nga la pynkhawai ïa ka kali jong phi.
n: Flag: tieng (be scared) is a safe choice; 'panic' is used as a loan too.

t: ban shim ïa [noun] kumba ka dei shaphang jong phi
ex: Wat shim ïa ka kumba ka dei shaphang jong phi. U long kumta bad baroh.
Map ïa nga lada nga la pynsngewsih ïa phi.
n: pynsngewsih = make someone feel hurt.

t: ban sngew ba la ïeh noh
ex: Ai ruh ïa ka para jong phi, lymda kan sngew ba la ïeh noh ïa ka.
n: Flag: descriptive (feel left behind).

ex: Ka la shim bun bnai shwa ba u la ïathuh ka mynsiem ïa nga.
n: mynsiem = heart, spirit.

t: ban pynmih ïa [noun] na ka mynsiem
ex: Nga donkam ban pynmih kawei ka kam na ka mynsiem jong nga.
n: Flag: calque-like but understood; plain: nga kwah ban ïathuh ïa phi kawei ka kam.

ex: Nga leit mareh hadien ka kam ban pynjem ïa ka jingsngew.
n: Flag: pynjem (make soft) is descriptive; many say 'release stress' in English.

ex: Nga sngew ar tylli shaphang ka jingwan biang sha ïing.
n: Flag: literal 'feel two ways'; ngam tip lada nga kmen ne em is plainer.

ex: Wow, ngam shym la ap ïa kata.
n: ap = wait for, expect.

ex: Nga la kular ban ïarap, bad ngam kwah ban pynsngewsih ïa ka.
n: Same verb as 'hurt feelings'; context gives 'let down'.

ex: Naduh hyndai nga burom ïa ka hynmen kynthei jong nga.
n: burom = honour, respect; hynmen = older sibling.

ex: Ngam tip kumno phi sah ïa kata ka jingsawa man ka miet.
n: Flag: sah (bear, stay with) chosen conservatively.

ex: Lada u bah u kylli, phin ïeng lang bad nga?
n: ïeng lang bad = stand together with.

ex: Baroh ar ki dei ki lok jong nga, te ngan ym ïeng ha kano kano ka liang.
n: liang = side.

ex: Nga bad u kpa ngim ju ïamynjur shaphang ka pisa.
n: ïa- makes it mutual: agree with each other.

ex: Nga dang ïadei bha bad u/ka jong nga ba barim.
n: Flag: 'my ex' has no neat Khasi term; adjust to context.

ex: Ngi la duh ka jingïadei hadien ka college.

t: ban pynrit khyndiat ka dor ïa [person]
ex: Ngam lah ban siew ka dor baroh, hynrei phi lah ban pynrit khyndiat ïa nga?
n: No halfway idiom; in a price haggle ask to lower it a little (pynrit).

ex: Ka la tip ba u la shukor ïa ka.
n: Flag: shukor (deceive) is the safe general verb; specific 'cheat on a partner' terms vary.

ex: U kwah ban leit kai katto katne snem shwa ba un shong kurim.
n: shong kurim = marry, settle down.

ex: Ngi kyrmen ban ioh khun hapoh ar snem.
Ka ïasyriem shisha bad u kpa jong ka. Kajuh ka jingrykhie.
n: ïasyriem = resemble.

ex: Baroh ki jrong. Ka long ha ka kur.
n: kur = clan; the natural Khasi frame for inherited traits.

ex: U hynmen jong nga u la ju sumar ïa nga ha skul.
Ki lok jong nga ki la pynmynjur ïa nga ban leit skydiving.
Kumba nga pyrkhat, ka kam ka la dep.
Wat sngewthuh bakla ïa nga, nga ieid ïa ka kam jong nga. Nga tang thait.
Ai nga sngewthuh beit. Phi la ïeh ïa ka kam mynhynnin?
Kaei? Ngam shym la sngewthuh.
n: Informal; Kaei? with a rise. To an elder say Map, phi la ong kaei?

ex: Ka pizza kaba bha tam ha ka nongbah? Ngan ym ong kumta.
Nga mynjur bad phi haduh shi jaka.
n: Flag: literal 'up to a place'; tang khyndiat (only partly) also works.

ex: Ha kawei ka liang, ban duh ïa kata ka kam ka la long kaba bha tam.
Ka jingpynkhreh ka la dor ar spah tyngka? Ka biang kumta.
n: Dollars adapted to rupees.

ex: Bha, nga sngewthuh. Ngan peit bha ha ka sien ba bud.
Ka lynti ka jngai, kata nga mynjur, hynrei ka jingïohi ka dor.
Nga tip ba ka sawa kum ka jingsniew, hynrei sngap khyndiat.
n: Informal; add sngewbha with elders.

ex: Bha, ka bank ka la ong em. Mynta ngi leh aiu?
Ap khyndiat. Don uwei ha ka jingkhang.
n: Flag: no idiom; 'wait a bit' pauses the point.

ex: Kata baroh na nga. Mynta ka dei phi, Sarah.
n: Literally 'now it is you'.

ex: Pizza bad ka phlim? Kata ka bha!
Oh, ka Wi-Fi ka la sangeh. Kumne biang.
n: Resigned tone; literally 'like this again'.

ex: Ka sngi Monday ka sniew tam. Wat ong!
n: Flag: 'don't say it' used as strong agreement; hooid shisha also works.

ex: Tang bud ïa ki jingpynshai. Kam eh.
n: Literally 'it isn't hard'.

ex: Kumba ngi kren shaphang jong ka, ka wan mynta.
n: No devil idiom; describe it: just as we speak of her, she comes.

t: Kumba kham bun, kumta kham bha
ex: Wallam ïa ki lok jong phi. Kumba kham bun, kumta kham bha!
n: kumba ... kumta ... = the more ... the more.

t: U Blei un kyrkhu ïa phi
ex: Ka show kaba heh mynta ka miet? U Blei un kyrkhu ïa phi!
n: No theatre idiom; a blessing or English 'All the best'.

ex: Ngam shym la pang lyngba u snem, wat ong eh.
n: Flag: no knock-on-wood custom; 'don't say it too loud' is the closest.

t: Nga kwah ban kyntiew ka glass na ka bynta
ex: Baroh, nga kwah ban kyntiew ka glass na ka bynta ki ar ngut kiba shong kurim.
n: Formal; kyntiew = raise.

ex: Na ka bynta ka weekend kaba jrong! Nga mynjur shisha!
n: No drinking formula; strong agreement.

t: Nga sngewsih shibun na ka bynta ka jingduh jong phi
ex: Nga la shu sngew shaphang u thawlang jong phi. Nga sngewsih shibun.
n: thawlang = grandfather. Keep it short and use phi.

ex: Ka kamra ka heh eh. Bad kaba kham, ka dor ka rit shisha.
Phi dei ban shim ka jacket, khamtam namar ba kan slap.
n: khamtam = especially.

ex: Ngam lah bha ban shet pasta, wat ka syiar baroh ruh ym.
n: wat ... ruh = even; the negative comes back.

ex: Namar ba phi ïeng, phi lah ban wallam khyndiat ka um?
n: Plain namar ba; no special 'seeing as' form.

ex: Ban thied ki juti kiba bha ka pynsumar pisa hadien jngai.
n: Flag: hadien jngai (far later) chosen conservatively.

ex: Ka kam thymmai kam kham eh. Ban kren shisha, ka kham suk.
n: Flag: no fixed 'if anything'; reframe with ban kren shisha.

ex: Ngan ïohi ïa phi ha ka sngi Tuesday, em, ha ka sngi Wednesday.
n: Self-correction with a plain em (no).

ex: Ngam tip lada ngan lah ban wan. Wat la kumno, ngan phone ïa phi.
Ngin leit sha duriaw lada kan slap ne em.
n: The ne em tag closes the clause.

ex: U bam ki jingbam kiba ym bha man ka sngi, hynrei um nang khia ei ei.
n: Plain hynrei; stress it for surprise.
